frase_gancho.texto: A city laid out with a ruler and with the sky.

introduccion_narrativa.texto: Before you take your first step, it helps to understand what you are standing on. Teotihuacán was the largest city in Mesoamerica, home to tens of thousands of people, and it was laid out with a precision that still astonishes: a grid rotated fifteen and a half degrees to align with the sky, a central avenue more than five kilometers long, and a river diverted to obey the plan. Almost none of the names you are about to hear belong to the people who built it, and its true name was lost. This first stop gives you the big picture from any entrance. After that, both the express route and the full route follow the Calzada de los Muertos from south to north.
